summary: The derivation mechanism is real and all five declared falsifications have teeth: I re-drove every one in a scratch copy at this HEAD and each reddened the row its field names, reproducing the producer's counts exactly (AC1 34/5, AC2 40/2, AC3 41/1, AC4 41/1, AC5 40/2). A genuine new pack arriving is covered (checked goes 3 -> 4, drift reds). Four things are false or unguarded, all measured by command. (1) THE READER CAN ANSWER WITH A VERSION THIS INSTALLATION IS NOT, WITH THE GATE GREEN, ON TWO INDEPENDENT PATHS. The canonical value is never shape-checked, so `"version": ""` in the marketplace makes `python3 .veldo/version.py` print ` (from .claude-plugin/marketplace.json)` and exit 0, --report exit 0 claiming agreement over three manifests, suite 42 passed 0 failed; and the AC4 row cannot fail in that state because it proves presence with `VV.version(ROOT)[0] in ok.stdout` and the empty string is a substring of everything. `_version_shaped` sits unused twenty lines below, applied only to proof bundles. Separately the canonical read is POSITIONAL: `plugins[0]` with no match on the name `veldo` that is right there in the entry, so a marketplace whose veldo entry declares 3.11.0 behind one co-hosted entry declaring 3.10.1 makes the reader answer 3.10.1, exit 0, suite green, and --report never mentions 3.11.0. (2) THE MEASURED GAP THAT JUSTIFIES THE ITEM IS FALSE. packs/antigravity/plugin.json was already guarded before this item by a DERIVED check, WARP-1311 AC5 in scripts/suites/01_warp_0101_reviewer_notes.py, which enumerates every marketplace plugin ENTRY plus packs/*/plugin.json and packs/*/.claude-plugin/plugin.json, requires at least three sites and one distinct value, and reds when antigravity drifts. It predates this item (`git show 1036e20^` carries it) and it catches the multi-entry case the new reader misses, so the new canonical read model is strictly weaker than the check the spec says it supersedes. (3) AC5's adopter is not real: `python3 .veldo/init_scaffold.py` lays down .veldo/version.py and NO .claude-plugin, so an adopting repository is VERSION_CANONICAL_ABSENT with the bare CLI exiting 1, not agreement over a set of one. The same file's drift() docstring states the truth and contradicts AC5 in the same module. (4) The declared fixtures exclusion is dead code whose row cannot fail: with its application deleted from both copies of version.py, the whole gate is GREEN (selftest 4530 passed, template sync pass, GATE: GREEN). None of the four needs more than a few lines to fix.

criteria.note: The mechanism is real and I proved it: `git ls-files` derivation, a new tracked pack manifest at packs/newtool/plugin.json is swept in without any test edit (report goes to '4 manifest(s) checked'), drifting it to 3.10.2 reds the AC3 live row, and the declared falsification has teeth (hand-written pair substituted for the sweep, proven by diff, suite 34 passed 5 failed with the antigravity row and the anti-vacuity row both named). REFUTED on two counts of what the criterion TEXT states. First, its MEASURED sentence is false: 'the only assertion covering them named TWO, so packs/antigravity/plugin.json was unguarded'. WARP-1311 AC5 in scripts/suites/01_warp_0101_reviewer_notes.py already derived every version site including packs/antigravity/plugin.json, asserted at least three of them and one distinct value, and it predates this item - `git show 1036e20^:scripts/suites/01_warp_0101_reviewer_notes.py` contains it, and setting antigravity to 9.9.9 at this HEAD reds it (suite 01: 624 passed, 1 failed) with all three sites printed in the row. The hand-listed PAIR the spec quotes (WARP-1508 AC4, line 1547) is a second, weaker assertion that coexists with the derived one. Second, 'EVERY MANIFEST THAT DECLARES A VERSION IS DERIVED' is not what the code does: the FILE set is derived, but a second version DECLARATION inside the canonical file itself is invisible (see F2), and the sweep derives over a hand-listed pair of FILENAMES (MANIFEST_NAMES), so README.md's tracked 'Current plugin version: 3.10.1' is a declaration nothing checks (see F7).

Confirmed for the triggers the criterion names, and driven: replacing the absent-canonical branch with `return "0.0.0", None, None` (diff proven) reds the named AC2 row and the AC4 row (40 passed, 2 failed); an unreadable canonical manifest refuses the same way; the negative control returns the real version with no cause. The refusal is real, not the reader's only answer. WITH THIS HOLE, recorded here and filed as F1 rather than as a pass: the refusal is keyed on `v is None` alone, so a canonical manifest that declares `""` or `"TBD"` is not a refusal at all - version() returns it, the CLI exits 0 and the suite is green (42 passed, 0 failed in both cases). An empty identity reported as an answer is the confident-zero disease this criterion names, one branch away from being closed by `_version_shaped`, which already exists in the same module.

Driven twice. Keeping the dict keys but collapsing the detail string to 'the versions differ' reds the named AC3 row (41 passed, 1 failed); dropping the keys entirely reds AC3 through its block wrapper. The record carries manifest, declares, canonical, canonical_declares and a detail naming both values, report_lines prints both, and an unparseable manifest is a separate finding from a disagreement (verified over a temp tree). TWO CAVEATS, both filed. The blame can be inverted rather than merely uninformative: with a co-hosted marketplace entry listed first at 1.0.0, the report names both veldo packs as disagreeing with a number that is not veldo's (F2). And the live row requires `disagreements == []` and `unparseable == []` over LIVE repository state, so committing a file named exactly plugin.json outside a directory literally named fixtures reds the gate (F6, demonstrated).

Driven: making the bare CLI print '3.10.1' and return 0 when the canonical declaration is absent reds the named AC4 row (41 passed, 1 failed), and the row is a real subprocess run, so the exit status is genuinely under test. At this HEAD the CLI prints '3.10.1 (from .claude-plugin/marketplace.json)' and exits 0, and in a temp tree with no canonical file it prints VERSION_CANONICAL_ABSENT and exits 1 with no version-shaped string in stdout. THE CRITERION'S CLOSING GUARANTEE DOES NOT HOLD and is filed as F1: 'a script that captures its output can never silently receive a guess' is defeated by a canonical `"version": ""`, where the script receives ' (from .claude-plugin/marketplace.json)' and exit 0; and the row's own presence clause, `VV.version(ROOT)[0] in ok.stdout`, is a substring scan that cannot fail in exactly that state because the empty string is a substring of every string.

The mechanical property is real and has teeth: dropping `rep["checked"] = len(manifests)` and the count from report_lines reds the named AC5 row and the AC3 negative control (40 passed, 2 failed); a temp tree with only a canonical manifest reports checked 1, cause None, no disagreements, and the line '1 manifest(s) checked'; the report carries one key shape whether it refused or not, over the live tree and over a nonexistent tree. REFUTED on the case the criterion names. 'An adopting repository has a canonical declaration and no packs, so the sweep finds one manifest' is false about the shipped scaffolder: I ran `python3 .veldo/init_scaffold.py` into a fresh git repo (60 files created, substrate complete), and the tree has no .claude-plugin at all, so `python3 .veldo/version.py` there prints VERSION_CANONICAL_ABSENT and EXITS 1 while .veldo/installed.json in the same tree records version 3.10.1. The suite row repeats the false claim to a future reader ('which is what an adopting repository looks like'), and drift() in the same file states the opposite ('A scaffolded repository carries the STAMP but no marketplace manifest - it is not a marketplace'), printed verbatim by `--drift` in that tree: 'An adopting repository is always in this state, because it is not a marketplace'. So the tree the criterion is justified by is covered by AC2/AC4's refusal path, not by AC5's set of one.

findings.text: THE CANONICAL VERSION IS NEVER SHAPE-CHECKED, SO AN EMPTY OR NON-VERSION STRING IS REPORTED AS THIS INSTALLATION'S IDENTITY WITH EXIT 0 AND A GREEN GATE. version() refuses only when `v is None`; read_manifest accepts any `str`. With every manifest declaring "TBD" the CLI prints 'TBD (from .claude-plugin/marketplace.json)' and exits 0. With every manifest declaring "" the CLI prints ' (from .claude-plugin/marketplace.json)' and exits 0, --report prints 'veldo version:  (canonical: .claude-plugin/marketplace.json), 3 manifest(s) checked' and exits 0, and the suite is green in both cases. That defeats AC4's stated guarantee that a script capturing the output can never silently receive a guess: it receives an empty version and a zero exit, which reads as a pass. It is unfalsifiable from inside the suite because the AC4 row proves presence with a substring scan, `VV.version(ROOT)[0] in ok.stdout`, and the empty string is a substring of every string, so that clause cannot fail in the one state where it matters. The fix is one call to `_version_shaped`, which already exists in this module and is applied only to proof bundles.
findings.evidence: In a clean copy of this HEAD (scratchpad/l2-0008-attackB): set the version field of .claude-plugin/marketplace.json plugins[0] and both pack manifests to 'TBD' -> `python3 .veldo/version.py` => 'TBD (from .claude-plugin/marketplace.json)', exit=0; `python3 scripts/selftest.py --suite 25_veldo_0008_version` => 'selftest (PARTIAL, 1 of 34 suites): 42 passed, 0 failed'. Then set all three to '' -> bare CLI stdout between markers: '[ (from .claude-plugin/marketplace.json)]', exit=0; `python3 .veldo/version.py --report` => 'veldo version:  (canonical: .claude-plugin/marketplace.json), 3 manifest(s) checked' with three blank version columns, report exit=0; suite => '42 passed, 0 failed'.

findings.text: THE CANONICAL READ IS POSITIONAL, NOT BY IDENTITY: _declared_version takes `plugins[0]` and never matches the entry named 'veldo', which is in the manifest. A marketplace with one co-hosted entry listed first therefore makes the reader answer a version the veldo plugin does not declare, and the report collapses a multi-entry marketplace to one number, hiding the real entry. Two measured shapes: (a) companion 1.0.0 first, veldo 3.10.1 second -> the CLI answers '1.0.0', exit 0, and --report names BOTH veldo packs as the ones disagreeing with the canonical declaration, which is the inverse of the diagnosis AC3 promises; (b) companion 3.10.1 first, the veldo entry bumped to 3.11.0 (the number an adopter installs) -> the CLI answers '3.10.1', exit 0, --report claims agreement over 3 manifests, never mentions 3.11.0, and THE SUITE IS GREEN. Also, a top-level "version" key in the marketplace manifest shadows plugins[0] entirely, so a schema version there is answered as the product version ('1 (from .claude-plugin/marketplace.json)', exit 0). The pre-existing WARP-1311 AC5 iterates every plugin entry and reds on (b), so on this axis the new canonical read model is strictly weaker than the assertion the spec says it supersedes.
findings.evidence: Clean copy of this HEAD. (a) inserted {"name":"veldo-companion","version":"1.0.0"} first: `python3 .veldo/version.py` => '1.0.0 (from .claude-plugin/marketplace.json)' exit=0; `--report` => 'VERSION_DISAGREEMENT: packs/antigravity/plugin.json declares '3.10.1' but the canonical declaration .claude-plugin/marketplace.json declares '1.0.0'' (and the same for packs/claude). (b) companion first at 3.10.1 with the veldo entry at 3.11.0: entries read [('veldo-companion','3.10.1'),('veldo','3.11.0')]; CLI => '3.10.1 (from .claude-plugin/marketplace.json)' exit=0; `--report` => 'veldo version: 3.10.1 ... 3 manifest(s) checked' exit=0; `python3 scripts/selftest.py --suite 25_veldo_0008_version` => '42 passed, 0 failed'; `python3 scripts/selftest.py --suite 01_warp_0101_reviewer_notes` => 'SELFTEST FAIL: WARP-1311 AC5 ... (sites: ['.claude-plugin/marketplace.json:veldo', '.claude-plugin/marketplace.json:veldo-companion', 'packs/antigravity/plugin.json', 'packs/claude/.claude-plugin/plugin.json'])', 624 passed 1 failed. Top-level key: added "version": "1" to the marketplace object -> CLI => '1 (from .claude-plugin/marketplace.json)' exit=0.

findings.text: THE MEASURED GAP THAT JUSTIFIES THE ITEM IS FALSE, IN FOUR PLACES INCLUDING THE GATE'S OWN OUTPUT. The spec body says 'The third has never been checked by anything', AC1's text says 'the only assertion covering them named TWO, so packs/antigravity/plugin.json was unguarded', .veldo/version.py's module docstring says 'so packs/antigravity/plugin.json had never been checked by anything', and the AC1 suite row prints 'a third declaration of this project's version that NOTHING checked before this item' every time the gate runs. WARP-1311 AC5 in scripts/suites/01_warp_0101_reviewer_notes.py already covered it, and covered it by DERIVATION: it walks every plugin entry of .claude-plugin/marketplace.json plus the globs packs/*/plugin.json and packs/*/.claude-plugin/plugin.json, and asserts at least three sites with exactly one distinct value. Its own comment says it was written to replace a hardcoded pair for this exact reason. So the item's premise (this repository shipped the hand-listed-pair defect a third time here) is wrong: what existed was a derived check plus a redundant weaker pair (WARP-1508 AC4). This matters beyond bookkeeping, because the false premise is what makes a strictly weaker replacement look like a strengthening (see F2).
findings.evidence: `git show 1036e20^:scripts/suites/01_warp_0101_reviewer_notes.py | grep -n 'every manifest that declares a plugin version'` => line 2562 present at the commit BEFORE VELDO-0008 (1036e20), and the glob line 'for _w13_pat in ("packs/*/plugin.json", "packs/*/.claude-plugin/plugin.json")' at 2557. That file's last change is c3810f4, older than 1036e20, so the check at HEAD is the check that predates the item. Teeth proven at this HEAD in a clean copy: set packs/antigravity/plugin.json version to 9.9.9 -> `python3 scripts/selftest.py --suite 01_warp_0101_reviewer_notes` => 'SELFTEST FAIL: WARP-1311 AC5 ... (sites: ['.claude-plugin/marketplace.json:veldo', 'packs/antigravity/plugin.json', 'packs/claude/.claude-plugin/plugin.json'])', 624 passed 1 failed.

findings.text: AC5 IS JUSTIFIED BY AN ADOPTER THAT DOES NOT EXIST, AND THE MODULE CONTRADICTS ITSELF ABOUT IT. AC5 says 'An adopting repository has a canonical declaration and no packs, so the sweep finds one manifest and the honest report is agreement over a set of ONE', and the suite row repeats it ('which is what an adopting repository looks like'). The shipped scaffolder lays down .veldo/version.py and no .claude-plugin at all, so a real adopting repository is VERSION_CANONICAL_ABSENT: the bare CLI exits 1 and answers nothing, in the tree where 'what this installation is' is the whole question, while .veldo/installed.json in that same tree records 3.10.1 and only `--drift` will say so. drift()'s docstring in the same file states the truth ('A scaffolded repository carries the STAMP but no marketplace manifest - it is not a marketplace'), so one module asserts both. The consequence for the review record is that AC5's row tests a synthetic one-manifest tree that nothing in the field produces, and the real adopter state is covered by AC2/AC4 instead.
findings.evidence: Clean copy of this HEAD: `git init` an empty dir, `python3 .veldo/init_scaffold.py <dir>` => 'created 60 file(s), skipped 0 existing / substrate complete'. In that tree: `ls .claude-plugin` => 'No such file or directory'; `python3 .veldo/version.py` => 'veldo version: VERSION_CANONICAL_ABSENT - the canonical declaration .claude-plugin/marketplace.json is absent...', exit=1; `--report` same, exit=1; `cat .veldo/installed.json` => {"version": "3.10.1", "schema": "veldo.installed/v1", ...}; `--drift` => 'VERSION_NOTHING_TO_COMPARE - ... An adopting repository is always in this state, because it is not a marketplace', exit=0. Also `grep -n version.py .veldo/init_scaffold.py` shows '.veldo/version.py' in the lay-down list and no marketplace manifest anywhere in it.

findings.text: THE DECLARED FIXTURES EXCLUSION IS DEAD CODE AND ITS ROW CANNOT FAIL. The AC1 row asserts 'fixture manifests are EXCLUDED with their reason declared' by two clauses that are both satisfied without the exclusion existing: `not any('fixtures' in Path(rel).parts for rel in live)`, which holds because the tracked fixtures are named pass.plugin.json and fail.plugin.json and the NAME filter already drops them, and `VV.EXCLUDE_PARTS == ('fixtures',)`, which is a literal comparison against a constant. Nothing constructs a fixture manifest and proves it is excluded. Deleting the two lines that apply EXCLUDE_PARTS from BOTH copies of version.py leaves the whole gate GREEN. This is a claimed exclusion that is a claim about code, with no behavioural check behind it, and the residual it hides is F6.
findings.evidence: Copy A (both copies mutated, byte-identical so template sync passes): removed 'if any(part in EXCLUDE_PARTS for part in Path(rel).parts): continue' from .veldo/version.py and engine/.veldo/version.py -> `bash scripts/verify.sh` => 'selftest: 4530 passed, 0 failed', 'template sync: pass (122 pair(s) compared...)', 'GATE: GREEN (dda45bff3e86fb336f5899f37ed6678a42ce06b6)', EXIT=0. Copy with only the root file mutated: gate RED, but solely on 'FAIL: .veldo/version.py drifted from engine/.veldo/version.py', which any edit trips. `grep -rn EXCLUDE_PARTS --include=*.py .` => only the two module copies and the literal comparison in scripts/suites/25_veldo_0008_version.py:73.

findings.text: THE AC3 LIVE ROW REQUIRES TWO SETS OVER LIVE REPOSITORY STATE TO BE EMPTY, so it reds the first time somebody commits a file named exactly plugin.json that is not a declaration of this project's version. The sweep equates 'a tracked file named plugin.json or marketplace.json' with 'a declaration of THIS project's version', and the only escape hatch is a path component spelled exactly 'fixtures'. A plugin-load runner sample or any vendored third-party manifest under, say, testdata/ reds the gate with a message claiming this repository's version manifests disagree. This tree already carries tool-schema versions of exactly that kind (packs/cursor/.cursor/hooks/hooks.json declares "version": 1), and the plugin runner's default manifest name is literally plugin.json.
findings.evidence: Clean copy of this HEAD: created engine/scripts/runners/plugin/testdata/plugin.json containing {"name": "third-party-sample", "version": "1.0.0"}, `git add` it -> `python3 scripts/selftest.py --suite 25_veldo_0008_version` => 'SELFTEST FAIL: VELDO-0008 AC3 OVER THE LIVE TREE: every derived manifest AGREES with the canonical declaration...', 41 passed 1 failed; `python3 .veldo/version.py --report` => '4 manifest(s) checked' with 'VERSION_DISAGREEMENT: engine/scripts/runners/plugin/testdata/plugin.json declares '1.0.0' but the canonical declaration ... declares '3.10.1''. The name filter, not the exclusion, is what keeps the existing fixtures/pass.plugin.json out.

findings.text: A FOURTH TRACKED DECLARATION OF THE NUMBER IS UNGUARDED, because the sweep derives file paths but hand-lists FILENAMES. README.md line 68 says 'Current plugin version: 3.10.1' and nothing reads it, so the next release bumps three manifests and leaves the sentence an adopter reads first behind. It is mitigated by its own parenthetical ('the manifests are the source of truth'), which is why this is a note rather than a defect in the number, but it is the same shape the item exists to remove: a copy of the version maintained by memory. MANIFEST_NAMES = ('plugin.json', 'marketplace.json') is the list that a fifth declaration shape (an extension manifest, a pyproject, a docs line) escapes through.
findings.evidence: `git grep -n '3\.10\.1'` lists README.md:68 alongside the three manifests (plus generated artifacts .veldo/last_verify and the proof manifests). `grep -rn 'Current plugin version' --include=*.py --include=*.sh .` => no matches, and `grep -rn README scripts/suites/*.py scripts/*.py .veldo/*.py | grep -iE 'version|3\.10'` => no matches, so no check reads it.
